title: QMM Ilmenite Mine, Fort Dauphin
place: Mandena, near Taolagnaro (Fort Dauphin), Anosy, Madagascar

lenders.name: MIGA
lenders.role: Issued a $3.3 million guarantee (board approval set for 23 October 2008) against breach of contract, for up to 10 years, to QIT Madagascar Minerals Ltd for the sixth generator in QMM's power plant. That generator was added to sell power to the town of Fort Dauphin; the other five supply the mine and port. MIGA says this falls within the World Bank-supported Integrated Growth Poles Project. MIGA lists the project as not active.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA), Integrated Growth Poles Project
lenders.role: The Integrated Growth Poles Project (P083351) was approved on 12 July 2005, became effective on 28 September 2005 and closed on 31 December 2014 against an original closing date of 31 December 2010. It was financed by credits IDA-41010 and IDA-43990, with an original commitment of SDR 85.90 million revised to SDR 107.56 million and SDR 107.31 million disbursed; the additional credit of SDR 25 million (US$40 million) was approved by the Bank's board in April 2008 and the financing agreement signed on 8 May 2008. The project covered Antananarivo-Antsirabe, Nosy Be and Taolagnaro (Fort Dauphin). Its Fort Dauphin component built a new public port on the Ehoala peninsula under a public-private partnership with Rio Tinto and part-rehabilitated the existing port. The Bank's completion report lists, among the component's safeguards activities, 'implementation of RAPs for the QMM's mining facility and Ehoala Port' and water supply and sanitation schemes for project-affected people. Because the Bank financed Ehoala Port as an associated investment supporting Rio Tinto's mining, Rio Tinto also had to comply with Bank safeguard policies. The project was environmental category A and an independent expert advisory panel monitored safeguards compliance during preparation and implementation (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 15 June 2015).
